title.narrative: Supporting early response and agricultural livelihood recovery of smallholders affected by Tropical Cyclone Trami in Camarines Sur

description.narrative: FAO's rapid response initiative strengthens the humanitarian response in Camarines Sur by employing a combination of phased strategic interventions to meet the immediate needs of 1,000 affected farmers and then help rebuild their livelihood. The first phase involves unconditional cash transfer which will be provided to the farmers to support their immediate household needs. The one-off unconditional Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) is based on the Cash Working Group’s Guidance Note on Temporary Expenditure Basket and Cash Transfer Value (CTV) amounting to Php12,000 (US$203) in Region V.Aside from the MPCA, the second phase of the project will utilize Cash+ wherein FAO provides conditional cash transfer (Cash for Work), necessary productive assets or inputs, and/or technical training and activities to enhance the livelihoods and productive capacities of the same 1,000 partner-farmers. The details of the Cash+ will be based on a needs assessment wherein the farmers will define the types of support they need to restore their livelihoods. If Cash for Work is deemed necessary by the farmers, the basis of the cash transfer value will be the Regional Daily Minimum Wage as per 2023 Guideline for Implementers of Cash for Work in the Philippines.The unconditional cash component enables farmer beneficiaries' households to address their immediate basic needs, including for food, while the Cash+ component supports investment in household production, helping to protect, restore and develop livelihoods which may include provision of agricultural inputs and seedlings.
